description:
OpenAI is growing faster than almost any technology company in history. It’s also burning through cash at an extraordinary rate.

In 2025, OpenAI generated more than $13 Billion in revenue, but its operating costs reached roughly $34 Billion. At the same time, it committed hundreds of billions more to chips, data centers, cloud infrastructure, and future computing capacity. So who ultimately pays for it?
The answer may go far beyond ChatGPT subscriptions. OpenAI’s expansion is increasingly tied to Nvidia, Microsoft, Oracle, power grids, private investors, and eventually public markets. That means the cost of the AI race can show up through higher electricity bills, retirement portfolios, corporate losses, and potentially government incentives.

OpenAI may still become one of the most valuable companies ever built, but if the economics don’t work, someone will be left holding the bill.

description:
Scientists are beginning to question whether space and time are fundamental parts of reality at all.

Quantum entanglement showed that particles can remain correlated across enormous distances, challenging Einstein’s idea of local realism. Then physicists pushed the experiment into space. In the Cosmic Bell Test, light from quasars billions of light-years away was used to determine how entangled particles would be measured, closing one of the biggest remaining loopholes in Bell experiments. The results still supported quantum mechanics.
That leaves physicists confronting some deeply strange possibilities. Either reality is fundamentally nonlocal, space-time emerges from a deeper quantum structure, or everything, including our choices, was predetermined from the beginning.

Space and time may feel fundamental to us, but quantum physics suggests they might not be.
